name: Linux Kernel Memory Model
description: An axiomatic (cat/herd7) model for the Linux kernel's own concurrency primitives — READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE, smp_mb()/smp_rmb()/smp_wmb()/smp_store_release()/smp_load_acquire(), RCU, and locking. Deliberately defined as a weak 'virtual architecture' so that code verified against it is sound on every CPU the kernel supports (x86, ARM, POWER, RISC-V, …). Notably formalises RCU grace-period ordering, which language standards such as C11 do not express.

catSupport.note: linux-kernel.cat, maintained in the kernel tree (tools/memory-model) and run by herd7 — the model was written in cat from the start, with kernel.cfg/kernel.def shipped by herdtools7.

katSupport.note: kater's kat/lkmm2.kat states LKMM's axioms in the fragment but is written over internal (-imm) relations, which kater rejects in every mode — including when that file is the one it was handed — so as shipped it is neither a comparison operand nor a checking target. The relations it redefines from their -imm counterparts (po, po-loc, mo, fr, rmw, ctrl, addr, data) are all in kater's builtin theory, so litmus/kater/derive-lkmm.sh restates it over those at run time; comparisons run against that derived file, not the shipped one. Its endpoints are untyped where IMM's are ([ACQ];po, not [R];(deps)+;[W]), which is what still blocks the LKMM compilation edges — see litmus/kater/open/compilation-LKMM-vs-x86-TSO.kat.
